# FDG5094

> DO only implement inequality operators on types that implement `IComparable<T>`.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 5.7.3 Inequality Operators.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (full coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDG5094
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: verified

Message: Implement IComparable<{0}> on '{0}', which defines inequality operators

FDG5094 reports, once per type, an externally visible class or struct that declares operator <, >, <= or >= and does not implement IComparable<T> with T the type itself. Interfaces are not reported. The body of FDG5095 says that a type with the operators has an easy basis for implementing the interface; adding an interface changes no existing signature, so the fix is not breaking, but there is no code fix. CA1036 is not mapped: it asks a type that implements IComparable to define all the comparison operators, the opposite direction, which the text does not ask.
